maya li: Heads-up — saw a weird regression on the INT8 KV path during the late-night perf run. p95 token time jumped ~40% for a subset of long-context chats.
jonah r: ah, details? which model / kernel / batch shape?
maya li: llama2-13b-8k, mixed-precision routing (FP8 decode, INT8 KV). Most traffic 1-4 tokens/sec small bursts. The spike correlates with KV occupancy ~70% and a sudden switch to large micro-batches (due to backlog).
alex c: do you have profiler traces? nvprof / nsight or our runtime flame?
maya li: pasted a short extract below. notice the repeated memcpy + kernel fallback loop.
```
[2026-03-17 03:12:05] REQUEST 0x7f8a: seq_len_in 64, kv_bytes 4.8MB, selected_kernel=int8_kv_dec
[2026-03-17 03:12:05] KERNEL_RUN int8_kv_dec (ms)=0.8, memcpy_host2dev (ms)=1.2
[2026-03-17 03:12:05] EVICT slab0 idx 23 (reason=compactness_crossing)
[2026-03-17 03:12:05] KERNEL_SWITCH to fp8_kv_safe (ms)=2.9
[2026-03-17 03:12:05] DECODE step total (ms)=6.3  <-- much higher than baseline 2.1ms
```
jonah r: weird. "compactness_crossing" evict sounds like our slab defrag kicking in under INT8 layout. Could be quantized KV pages misaligned so memcpy becomes non-coalesced.
kevin: also check calibration drift. If INT8 scales were derived offline on shorter sequences, the distribution tail for 8k contexts can underflow/overflow and break our fast path. That forces safe path + copies.
tia: I think we saw something similar in canary last month but it was transient. Does the effect persist after warmup?
maya li: yes, persists for ~10-20min once a backlog triggers a kernel swap. After manual evictions it returns to normal.
jonah r: hypothesis: batching heuristic treats these small requests as opportunity to fill large micro-batches. Combined with high KV occupancy, the runtime tries to pack many keys into INT8 slabs -> fragmentation -> non-contiguous GPU pages -> memcpy thrash + kernel fallback.
alex c: makes sense. two levers: (1) adjust batching policy to prefer latency over packing when kv_occupancy > threshold; (2) add a KV-layout-aware hysteresis so we don't switch to compacting slab immediately under transient backlog.
kevin: +1. Also add a metric: kv_eviction_rate and kv_page_copy_time to surface this earlier.
tia: any quick repro harness? can run a synthetic workload.
maya li: yes, I have a repro script that simulates 1-3 token bursts with 6ms inter-arrival jitter. Dropped here:
```
# repro: stress_kv_swap.py (concept)
for t in range(10000):
  send_request(seq_len=64, tokens=1..4)
  sleep(random.uniform(0.004,0.01))
```
Running on a single GPU with int8_kv quantization shows p95 6.5ms -> 9.2ms when slab defrag triggers.
jonah r: config proposal (pseudo):
```
batching:
  mode: latency_prefer
  max_microbatch_tokens: 1024
  kv_occupancy_hysteresis_pct: 15  # don't compact if occupancy jumps <15%
kv:
  prefer_fp8_for_small_keys_below: 2MB
  eviction_grace_ms: 200
```
alex c: Also kernel selection change: prefer fp8_kv_safe if kv_page_copy_time > 0.5ms average for last 1m. That avoids repeated switchbacks.
kevin: we should probably avoid changing default quantization without eval — add a short AB test on Dedicated nodes. Canary config -> group A keep int8_kv, group B prefer fp8_kv_safe under occupancy. Measure token-cost delta and decode-quality diff (regressions).
maya li: rolled an experimental canary to 10% traffic on ded-1, capturing kv_eviction_rate, p50/p95 token_time, and decode-token-delta (LLM perplexity on eval set). Early data: eviction_rate dropped x4 and p95 down 30% for the affected workload. No quality regress yet.
tia: nice. can you paste the dashboard query?
maya li: quick Grafana panels:
- sum(rate(kv_evictions[1m])) by node
- histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(token_latency_bucket[5m]))
- avg_over_time(kv_page_copy_time[1m])
jonah r: next steps:
1) land batching heuristic change behind flag (runtime switch)
2) add kv_eviction_rate metric + page copy timer
3) run A/B for 48h on dedicated pool
4) if stable, bake into kernel selection policy (avoid oscillation)
kevin: add unit test for slab layout alignment (simulate fragmentation) and runner that asserts kernel_switch_count <= 3 under steady load.
alex c: I'll open a PR for the heuristic. tagging @kevin for metric PR and @tia for canary plan.
infra-bot: deploy scheduled: staging/runtime/kv-hysteresis -> 2026-03-17T08:00:00Z (CI: green).
maya li: thanks all. I'll attach profiler captures + repro script in the issue. If anyone wants to pair on kernel selector logic ping me. :thumbsup:
kevin: thanks maya, this explains a lot of the Friday noise. :coffee:
